text:
The suspect should be found **not guilty** if the jury believes his version. The statute only bars force in resisting an arrest, and on his account the officer answered mere cursing with a nightstick, which is excessive force. A person may use reasonable force to defend against that, even against an officer, so the team note is wrong to say any blow is a crime in either version. If the jury believes the officer, the suspect struck first and would be guilty, so the verdict turns on whose account is credited.

CONFIDENCE: 72
